notes: The circuit image shows the breadboard with rows f-j at the top and a-e at the bottom, so the catalogue's 'b' bank (f-j) is the upper half and its 't' bank (a-e) is the lower half. The rails next to the lower half are therefore tp/tn, with tp as the + rail and tn as the - rail.

Column numbers and rail hole indices were estimated from pixel positions in the image. The button sits in columns 4 and 6, the resistor in columns 6 and 9, and the rail holes are indexed 1-5 and 6-10 in the two groups.
Button side pairing: 1.l and 1.r are the two legs in column 4 (the 5V side). 2.l and 2.r are the two legs in column 6 (the pin 2 / pull-down side).

Pin 2 connects to the column-6 strip on the upper half, which joins the button leg. The pull-down resistor is on the lower-half column-6 strip, which is joined through the button's side 2. The pull-down resistor therefore sits on the same side as the input pin, as the manual says.
The resistor is a 10k pull-down, so value=10000. No external LED is used, because the sketch drives the built-in LED on pin 13.
